fuller2015.label: Fuller et al. 2015
fuller2015.note: Found a significant positive association between shoe mass and metabolic cost, and no studies at all reporting effects on running performance as opposed to economy, as of April 2014.
fuller2015.source: Fuller JT, Bellenger CR, Thewlis D, Tsiros MD, Buckley JD (2015). The effect of footwear on running performance and running economy in distance runners. Sports Med 45(3):411-422.

ortega2021.label: Ortega et al. 2021
ortega2021.note: Puts the bending-stiffness literature at about 3% deterioration to about 3% improvement. The sign of the effect is not settled.
ortega2021.source: Ortega JA, Healey LA, Swinnen W, Hoogkamer W (2021). Energetics and Biomechanics of Running Footwear with Increased Longitudinal Bending Stiffness: A Narrative Review. Sports Med 51(5):873-894.

rodrigocarranza2022.label: Rodrigo-Carranza et al. 2022
rodrigocarranza2022.note: A curved plate improved economy 3.45% against no plate; a flat plate showed no improvement.
rodrigocarranza2022.source: Rodrigo-Carranza V, González-Mohíno F, Santos-Concejero J, González-Ravé JM (2022). The effects of footwear midsole longitudinal bending stiffness on running economy and ground contact biomechanics. Eur J Sport Sci 22(10):1508-1521.

stephen2025.label: Stephen et al. 2025
stephen2025.note: Neither longitudinal bending stiffness alone nor midsole energy return alone significantly affected oxygen consumption; only their interaction did. Quality of evidence graded low or very low for almost every outcome.
stephen2025.source: Stephen CHN, Kelly LA, Schuster RW, Diamond LE (2025). The effects of running shoe longitudinal bending stiffness and midsole energy return on oxygen consumption and ankle mechanics and energetics. J Sport Health Sci 14:101069.

xiao2025.label: Xiao et al. 2025
xiao2025.note: Also reports time-trial performance at g=-0.23, about half the size of the oxygen effect.
xiao2025.source: Xiao Y, Hu X, Tian D, Qiu A (2025). Effects of Advanced Footwear Technology on Running Economy and Endurance Performance: A Meta-Analysis. Int J Sports Med 47(2):81-94.

predicted.note: The laboratory range pushed through the transfer coefficient. Assumed: the coefficient was measured for added mass over 3000 m in trained men, not for advanced footwear over a marathon.

barnes2019_vaporfly_massmatched.comparison: Nike Vaporfly matched to Adios mass vs Adidas Adizero Adios 3
barnes2019_vaporfly_massmatched.note: The same pair of shoes as the 4.2% row with the mass difference removed. The gap between the two rows is what mass was worth.

barnes2019_vaporfly_vs_adios.comparison: Nike Vaporfly vs Adidas Adizero Adios 3
barnes2019_vaporfly_vs_adios.note: One of only two studies here with women in the sample. Against the same shoe mass-matched the figure is 2.9%, so about a third of this comparison is the Vaporfly being lighter rather than anything about its foam or plate.

barnes2019_vaporfly_vs_spike.comparison: Nike Vaporfly vs Nike Zoom Matumbo 3 track spike
barnes2019_vaporfly_vs_spike.note: The lower end of the individual range is negative: at least one runner was less economical in the shoe than in the control. The population mean and the individual outcome are different quantities and this row carries both.

guinness2020_men.comparison: Vaporfly vs not, marathon finishing time, men
guinness2020_men.note: Observational, not randomised: runners chose their own shoes and the fastest adopted them first. The interval is the result; there is no point estimate to draw.
guinness2020_men.setting: 22 marathons 2015-2019, shoes read from public race photographs

guinness2020_women.comparison: Vaporfly vs not, marathon finishing time, women
guinness2020_women.note: The women's interval from the same model.
guinness2020_women.setting: 22 marathons 2015-2019, shoes read from public race photographs

hoogkamer2016_mass_metabolic.note: The founding constant of the field, restated from Frederick, Daniels and Hayes 1984 and measured directly here. The one genuine confidence interval in this table.

hoogkamer2016_mass_time.comparison: +100 g per shoe, 3000 m time-trial time
hoogkamer2016_mass_time.note: The only row in the table measured as race time rather than as oxygen or energy cost. Its ratio to the metabolic row is the transfer coefficient the page uses, and labels assumed wherever it is applied to anything but added mass.

hoogkamer2018_proto_vs_adios.comparison: prototype vs Adidas Adizero Adios Boost, mass matched
hoogkamer2018_proto_vs_adios.note: The same prototype against the other established racing shoe.

hoogkamer2018_proto_vs_streak.comparison: prototype vs Nike Zoom Streak 6, mass matched
hoogkamer2018_proto_vs_streak.note: The origin of the 4% figure. A prototype rather than a retail shoe, mass-matched with lead, at three elite marathon paces. Reported as a mean with no dispersion.

hunter2019_vaporfly_vs_adios.comparison: retail Nike Vaporfly 4% vs Adidas Adizero Adios Boost
hunter2019_vaporfly_vs_adios.note: The consumer version of the shoe, measured by an independent group against the same control brand as the prototype study, at about two thirds of the prototype's benefit.

hunter2019_vaporfly_vs_streak.comparison: retail Nike Vaporfly 4% vs Nike Zoom Streak
hunter2019_vaporfly_vs_streak.note: The same retail shoe as the 2.8% row, against the other control.

joubert2024_spike_a.comparison: AFT track spike vs traditional track spike
joubert2024_spike_a.note: The first of two AFT spikes the study tested.

joubert2024_spike_b.comparison: second AFT track spike vs traditional track spike
joubert2024_spike_b.note: The second AFT spike in the same study. Included because the table's rule is every controlled comparison, and dropping the smaller of a study's two arms is how a collected table starts flattering itself.

joubert2026_trail.comparison: AFT trail shoe vs control trail shoe, outdoors
joubert2026_trail.note: The only row measured outside a laboratory, and the slowest. Its standard deviation equals its mean.

knopp2023_amateur.comparison: three AFT models vs a racing flat, per-athlete range
knopp2023_amateur.note: The comparison group in the same study.

knopp2023_kenyan.comparison: three AFT models vs a racing flat, per-athlete range
knopp2023_kenyan.note: The group the shoes were designed for, and the widest range anyone has published. Recorded as the paper states it: an 11.3% drawback to an 11.4% benefit.

rodrigocarranza2020_mass_85vt2.comparison: +100 g per shoe, energy cost at 85% of VT2
rodrigocarranza2020_mass_85vt2.note: Several times the accepted per-100 g figure, for the same manipulation. Peer-reviewed, not retracted, and rarely cited against the number it contradicts.

rodrigocarranza2020_mass_95vt2.comparison: +100 g per shoe, energy cost at 95% of VT2
rodrigocarranza2020_mass_95vt2.note: The same study's harder condition, further still from the accepted figure.

whiting2021_downhill.comparison: Nike Vaporfly 4% vs Nike Zoom Streak 6, -3 degrees
whiting2021_downhill.note: Not statistically distinguishable from the level condition in the paper, unlike the uphill one.

whiting2021_level.comparison: Nike Vaporfly 4% vs Nike Zoom Streak 6, level
whiting2021_level.note: Metabolic power rather than oxygen uptake. The level condition of the study that also ran it uphill and downhill.

whiting2021_uphill.comparison: Nike Vaporfly 4% vs Nike Zoom Streak 6, +3 degrees
whiting2021_uphill.note: Significantly smaller than the same study's level condition.

barnes2019.label: Barnes & Kilding 2019
barnes2019.source: Barnes KR, Kilding AE (2019). A Randomized Crossover Study Investigating the Running Economy of Highly-Trained Male and Female Distance Runners in Marathon Racing Shoes versus Track Spikes. Sports Med 49(2):331-342.

guinness2020.label: Guinness et al. 2020
guinness2020.source: Guinness J, Bhattacharya D, Chen J, Chen M, Loh A (2020). An Observational Study of the Effect of Nike Vaporfly Shoes on Marathon Performance. arXiv:2002.06105.

hoogkamer2016.label: Hoogkamer et al. 2016
hoogkamer2016.source: Hoogkamer W, Kipp S, Spiering BA, Kram R (2016). Altered Running Economy Directly Translates to Altered Distance-Running Performance. Med Sci Sports Exerc 48(11):2175-2180.

hoogkamer2018.label: Hoogkamer et al. 2018
hoogkamer2018.source: Hoogkamer W, Kipp S, Frank JH, Farina EM, Luo G, Kram R (2018). A Comparison of the Energetic Cost of Running in Marathon Racing Shoes. Sports Med 48(4):1009-1019 (correction, 48(6):1521-1522).

hunter2019.label: Hunter et al. 2019
hunter2019.source: Hunter I, McLeod A, Valentine D, Low T, Ward J, Hager R (2019). Running economy, mechanics, and marathon racing shoes. J Sports Sci 37(20):2367-2373.

joubert2024.label: Joubert et al. 2024
joubert2024.source: Joubert DP, Oehlert GM, Jones EJ, Burns GT (2024). Comparative Effects of Advanced Footwear Technology in Track Spikes and Road-Racing Shoes on Running Economy. Int J Sports Physiol Perform 19(7):705-711.

joubert2026.label: Joubert & Sanders 2026
joubert2026.source: Joubert DP, Sanders J (2026). Effects of Advanced Footwear Technology in Trail Running Shoes on Running Economy. J Strength Cond Res, ahead of print.

knopp2023.label: Knopp et al. 2023
knopp2023.source: Knopp M, Muñiz-Pardos B, Wackerhage H, Schönfelder M, Guppy F, Pitsiladis Y, Ruiz D (2023). Variability in Running Economy of Kenyan World-Class and European Amateur Male Runners with Advanced Footwear Running Technology. Sports Med 53(6):1255-1271.

rodrigocarranza2020.label: Rodrigo-Carranza et al. 2020
rodrigocarranza2020.source: Rodrigo-Carranza V, González-Mohíno F, Santos-Concejero J, González-Ravé JM (2020). Influence of Shoe Mass on Performance and Running Economy in Trained Runners. Front Physiol 11:573660.

whiting2021.label: Whiting et al. 2021
whiting2021.source: Whiting CS, Hoogkamer W, Kram R (2021). Metabolic cost of level, uphill, and downhill running in highly cushioned shoes with carbon-fiber plates. J Sport Health Sci 11(3):303-308.

transfer.note: The ratio of the two Hoogkamer 2016 rows: a 1% change in the metabolic cost of running bought this fraction of a percent in 3000 m time, for added shoe mass, in trained men. It has never been measured for advanced footwear.
